The building is an important civic landmark that symbolizes local governance and the city's development.

heritageItems.name: Ancestral Houses
heritageItems.description: The ancestral houses of Alaminos City are historic residential structures built by prominent families during the Spanish and American colonial periods. These houses showcase traditional Filipino architecture, featuring wooden materials, capiz shell windows, spacious interiors, and elevated designs adapted to the local climate. They reflect the cultural heritage, lifestyle, and craftsmanship of earlier generations in Alaminos.

The cathedral is an important religious, cultural, and historical landmark that reflects the faith and heritage of the local community. Its architecture and long-standing role in the city make it a significant heritage site.

heritageItems.name: Spirit of '96 Monument
heritageItems.description: The Spirit of '96 Monument is a historical landmark in Alaminos City that commemorates the bravery, patriotism, and sacrifices of local heroes who participated in the Philippine Revolution of 1896. The monument serves as a reminder of the city's contribution to the struggle for Philippine independence and stands as a symbol of national pride and historical remembrance.

heritageItems.name: Hundred Island
heritageItems.description: Hundred Islands National Park is the first national park in the Philippines and one of the most famous tourist destinations in Pangasinan. It consists of more than one hundred islands and islets scattered across the Lingayen Gulf. The park is known for its limestone formations, crystal-clear waters, diverse marine life, caves, beaches, and scenic landscapes, making it an important natural and cultural heritage site.

heritageItems.name: Parish Church of Our Lady of Lourdes Salasa
heritageItems.description: Old architectural design reflecting Spanish Colonial Revival Architectural Style. Its plastered brick façade was inspired by Mexican style. The pediment is flat-topped and decorated with massive pinnacles. The octagonal window, together with the semicircular door and windows, accentuates the plastered finish wall, its square pilaster reaching up to the roof are also decorated with pinnacles.  In March 2020, the face or front of the church was constructed and finished last November 2021. On top of the building are image of Our Lady of Lourdes and two angels and inaugurated last December 2021.

heritageItems.name: Major Jose Torres Bugallon Monument
heritageItems.description: The Major Jose Torres Bugallon Monument is a historical landmark located in Bugallon, Pangasinan. It honors Major Jose Torres Bugallon, a Filipino military officer and national hero who fought during the Philippine Revolution and the Philippine-American War. The monument commemorates his courage and patriotism and serves as a reminder of his contributions to the country's struggle for independence. The municipality itself was renamed from Salasa to Bugallon in 1921 in his honor.

heritageItems.description: The Governor Aguedo F. Agbayani Monument is a historical monument located within the Governor Aguedo F. Agbayani Park in Lingayen, Pangasinan. It honors the legacy of Governor Aguedo F. Agbayani, the longest-serving governor of Pangasinan, who served the province for a total of 17 years and contributed significantly to its development. The monument stands as a symbol of dedicated public service and leadership.

heritageItems.name: Giant Clam Capital
heritageItems.description: The Giant Clam Garden in Bolinao, Pangasinan is a marine conservation and research site dedicated to the protection, propagation, and restoration of giant clams (Tridacna species). Managed by the University of the Philippines Marine Science Institute, it has earned Bolinao the title "Giant Clam Capital of the Philippines" because of its successful giant clam conservation and breeding programs.

heritageItems.name: Cape Bolinao Light House
heritageItems.description: Cape Bolinao Lighthouse is one of the oldest operational lighthouses in the Philippines. Constructed during the Spanish colonial period in 1903, it stands on Punta Piedra Point overlooking the West Philippine Sea. The lighthouse has guided ships safely along the northwestern coast of Luzon for more than a century and is one of Bolinao's most recognizable historical landmarks.

heritageItems.name: Pangasinan Provincial Capitol building
heritageItems.description: The Pangasinan Provincial Capitol Building, located in Lingayen, serves as the official seat of the Provincial Government of Pangasinan. Constructed between 1917 and 1918 and designed by architect Ralph Harrington Doane in the French Neoclassical style, it is recognized as one of the Eight Architectural Treasures of the Philippines. In 2018, it was also declared a cultural heritage site by the Provincial Government of Pangasinan.

Visitors can also try surfing or simply swim in the usually calm waters of the beach.

The church was first managed by the Dominicans until 1898 before it was taken over by the Diocesan clergy until 1932. The compound is spacious so that anyone could take long walks and appreciate the solemn heritage that the mere existence of the church exudes.

heritageItems.name: Urdaneta Park Landmark Monument
heritageItems.description:
Aside from the “Metamorphosis,” a giant carabao monument, Urdaneta City boasts of another monument designed and created by four national artists, the “Urdaneta Park Landmark Monument.”
Unveiled in the year 2009, the monument is dedicated to Fray Andres de Urdaneta from whom the city was possibly named after. The event also marked the culmination of the 500th birth anniversary of Fray Urdaneta who accompanied the Loaísa expedition to the Spice Islands.
